name: Harper (formerly HarperDB)
tagline: Node.js runtime that fuses database, cache, app logic and MQTT/WebSocket messaging in one process.
description: Harper, called HarperDB until a 2025 rebrand, is a Node.js platform that runs the database, cache, application code and messaging in a single process so requests never cross a network hop. Tables are declared in GraphQL schema files and exported as REST endpoints automatically, data lives in LMDB or, since 5.0, RocksDB, and it adds secondary and HNSW vector indexes, caching with expiry, blob storage and publish/subscribe over MQTT, WebSockets and server-sent events. Harper 5.0 (April 2026) moved the core to Apache 2.0, while Harper Pro adds multi-node replication and certificate management under the Elastic License 2.0; Harper Fabric is the managed, geo-distributed offering. It fits latency-sensitive edge APIs and caches better than general relational workloads.
statusNote: Renamed from HarperDB to Harper in 2025; the open-source core is now the HarperFast/harper repository.

pricing.notes: Core is free; Harper Pro features are source-available; Harper Fabric is the managed service.

scale.notes: Single-node core; multi-node and geo-distributed replication come with Harper Pro or Harper Fabric.

strengths: Database, cache, application code and messaging share one process and memory space
Schema annotations generate REST endpoints with no boilerplate
Built-in MQTT and WebSocket pub/sub without a separate broker
LMDB and RocksDB storage engines with HNSW vector indexes
weaknesses: Replication and clustering sit in the ELv2-licensed Harper Pro, not the open-source core
Application logic must be written in JavaScript/Node.js
SQL support is limited compared with relational databases
Smaller community than Redis, MongoDB or Postgres
useCases: Edge caching and API acceleration in front of slower origins
Real-time apps needing MQTT or WebSocket fan-out
Vector lookups next to application logic
